entries.test: Public demonstrations and workflow studies showing whether contemporaneous ChatGPT and DALL-E products had practical uses would test the claim.
entries.note: The broad denial of practical usefulness has a testable plain reading.
Knowing anything has no shared operational meaning here; correct performance alone need not satisfy his conception of knowledge.
Image errors are observable, but the asserted cause depends on an undefined absence of knowledge.
Neither the relevant limits nor learning, understanding and intelligence receive a shared test.

entries.test: Public evaluations showing whether the described recurring image and hallucination failures can be reliably eliminated would test their asserted irreducibility.
entries.note: This asserts a present technical limitation with implications for future improvements.

entries.test: Published model architectures and controlled reliability evaluations would test whether prediction from dataset tags causes unavoidable hallucinations.
entries.note: The proposition centrally explains an alleged impossibility through a claimed mechanism.

entries.test: Controlled evaluations of hallucination rates and successful task completion across increasing task complexity would test the claim.
Representative audience studies and reception of released AI videos with visible hallucinations would show whether ordinary viewers find them deeply offensive.
entries.note: This predicts audience reactions, which are empirically measurable.
The proposition drops his belief framing and the claim about perfection. The asserted underestimation concerns companies' internal beliefs.
The proposition generalizes a statement about sign instructions to all prompt information. Knowledge and understanding remain undefined.

entries.test: Longitudinal public capability and accuracy evaluations would show whether generative AI's rapid improvements substantially plateau after publication.
entries.note: Rapidly approaching supplies no definite deadline, but a capability plateau has a plain reading.

entries.test: Contemporaneous task evaluations measuring how consistently Sora, Pika and other generative models fulfill specified requests would test their task competence.
Public production costs and audience reception of movies, shows or commercials assembled from inconsistent AI clips would test the claim.
entries.note: The cost assertion is implicit in 'even if the costs weren't prohibitive.'

entries.test: Published investments and evaluations of techniques reducing the discussed hallucination and consistency failures by February 2024 would test the claim.
entries.note: Context supplies concrete limitations despite the philosophical wording.
Calling this the greatest threat ranks harms without a specified evaluative standard.
Being at risk asserts a possibility of displacement rather than a definite outcome.

entries.test: Documented sustained replacement of media workers by generative AI and public records of failed replacement attempts would test the claim.
entries.note: The normalization drops 'the inevitable outcome,' turning a lasting prediction into a present observation.
Automating our existence supplies no shared scope or threshold for relevant practical evidence.

entries.test: Controlled business-copy workflows comparing total drafting and editing time with and without contemporary ChatGPT would test the claimed lack of clear time savings.
entries.note: The source discusses business copy; the normalization broadens this to all ChatGPT outputs.

entries.test: Public image samples across varied prompts and blinded assessments of visual similarity and detail errors would test the claim.
entries.note: The normalization strengthens 'all kind of look the same' to 'all look alike.'

entries.test: Public economic assessments establishing trillions of dollars in AI-created value alongside documented improvements to people's lives would test the proposed outcome.
entries.note: He expresses a skeptical position, but 'I don't argue it will' is weaker than a categorical prediction that it will not.

entries.test: Public economic assessments establishing trillions of dollars in AI-created value alongside documented improvements to people's lives would test the proposed outcome.
entries.note: The normalization turns withholding an affirmative prediction into a categorical negative prediction.

entries.test: Public capability and accuracy trends around publication and subsequent model releases would test whether generative AI was nearing a ceiling.
entries.note: The proposition removes the explicit 'I believe' qualification.

entries.test: A documented reassessment of AI's commercial capabilities followed by broad tech-sector financial damage would test the predicted industry-wide fallout.
entries.note: The proposition drops 'I believe'; the context gives the condition a commercial reading.
The normalization removes the central judgment that this threat should have smothered the companies early.

entries.test: Public incident reports and reliability evaluations would establish whether generative AI repeatedly produced incorrect or inappropriate outputs.
entries.note: The following examples make the claimed unreliability concrete.

entries.test: MSN staffing records and archived content before and after AI substitution would test whether the change caused fabricated and inaccurate publication.
entries.note: Destroyed is evaluative exaggeration, but the sentence supplies a concrete causal allegation.
'Doesn't seem' qualifies the conclusion as an appearance rather than a firm financial finding.

entries.test: Public ChatGPT web-traffic and mobile-usage estimates through January 2024 would establish whether the cited indicators of declining interest existed.
entries.note: This asserts the existence of indicators, not certainty about every consumer's interest.

entries.test: Public financial reporting comparing generative AI costs with revenues, together with reliability evaluations, would test the factual assertions.
entries.note: The metaphors do not erase the concrete claim of substantial losses.

entries.test: Provider financial disclosures and compute-cost breakdowns would show whether cloud expenses caused substantial generative AI losses.
entries.note: 'Likely' qualifies why reporting omits profitability, rather than the underlying assertion of unprofitability.

entries.test: Public gross-margin reports for AI model providers and conventional software companies would test the stated ranges.
entries.note: The figures appear in surrounding text as what reports suggest; the normalization presents them without that qualification.

entries.test: Public funding commitments, cloud contracts and financial disclosures would test whether cloud-provider backing insulated OpenAI and Anthropic from financial failure.
entries.note: Context identifies the risk as financial survival and explicitly supplies its alleged cause.

entries.test: Public investment agreements, cloud commitments and spending disclosures would establish whether the investments guaranteed revenue for the investing cloud providers.
entries.note: 'Must be spent' strengthens 'effectively obliged' into an unqualified requirement.

entries.test: Public AI spending breakdowns and cloud-provider revenue data would show how much growing AI expenditure flows to the named large technology companies.
Public hosting and billing arrangements for ChatGPT and Claude would show whether every interaction entails cloud-provider revenue.
entries.note: The proposition removes 'on some level,' which allows indirect revenue rather than an incremental payment for each interaction.

entries.test: Public cost measurements comparing webpage delivery with generative-model inference would test the asserted permanent cost ordering.
entries.note: A demonstrated reversal could refute the unrestricted 'always' claim.
The claim concerns investment motives, and the normalization drops the explicit inferential qualification for Amazon.

entries.test: Public AI-product spending and supplier-payment data would establish whether almost all AI spending eventually yields revenue for a few large technology firms.

entries.note: The source covers AI generally and explicitly excepts non-generative assistants. Essential and killer app lack a shared threshold here.
He reports his own difficulty identifying achievements; the proposition converts that private epistemic state into an objective claim.

entries.test: Contemporaneous product documentation and interfaces would show whether the cited translation capabilities were integrated features or standalone applications.

entries.note: This is an expressed comparative judgment about the hype cycles' merit.

entries.test: Public AI-industry revenues, costs and earnings at publication would test the central claim of deep unprofitability.
entries.note: Proving its worth is evaluative, but the financial assertion is concrete.

entries.test: Microsoft and Amazon capital-expenditure disclosures and data-center announcements would establish whether they were investing billions to serve AI demand.

entries.note: The proposition removes 'doesn't seem' and the stated exception for appeals to AI's future.

entries.test: Public lifecycle assessments comparing AI electricity-related environmental harms with demonstrated environmental benefits would test the claimed adverse balance.
entries.note: In context, this makes a factual environmental-impact assertion.

entries.test: Public customer-revenue breakdowns, integration adoption and retention data would test the providers' dependence on commercially useful business integrations.
entries.note: The central claim concerns an observable business dependency.

entries.test: Following a downturn among model-integrating startups, provider revenue disclosures and big-tech financing commitments would show whether revenue weakened and dependence increased.
entries.note: 'Main revenue stream' weakens the source's 'only real revenue stream.'
'Suggests' marks a tentative inference, preserved by 'likely'; worsening losses are conditional on rising revenue.
The normalization drops his emotional framing and the future concentration of big-tech power. The passage primarily expresses a judgment about waste and sustainability.
